scenes.text: The Hubble Space Telescope launched with a mistake thinner than a human hair.
Hubble went up on April twenty fourth, nineteen ninety.
Just two months later, NASA announced the telescope was flawed.
Its main mirror, about eight feet wide, had been ground slightly wrong.
The outer edge was too flat by about two microns, roughly one fiftieth the thickness of a hair.
That tiny error gave the mirror more than one focal point.
So light got scattered, and stars came out with fuzzy halos.
The cause? A testing tool with a lens spacing error of just one point three millimeters.
And that mistake had gone unnoticed since the mirror was ground in nineteen seventy nine.
So instead of replacing the mirror, engineers gave Hubble glasses.
In December nineteen ninety three, a seven person crew flew space shuttle Endeavour up to it.
They installed a device called COSTAR, with five pairs of corrective mirrors, some as small as a nickel.
They also swapped in a new main camera with its own built-in correction.
It worked, and Hubble has now made more than one and a half million observations.
Would you have trusted NASA again after that? Tell me below.

title: Hubble launched blurry. Astronauts gave it glasses 👓
caption: Hubble's 2.4 m mirror was ground about 2 microns too flat at the edge, so its first images were fuzzy. In December 1993 astronauts installed corrective optics, and it has made over 1.5 million observations since.
